content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

Terri Koch (E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes from team memory:
- HR agent: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment: admin not permitted because role doesn't own Payroll, max is write.
- Security agent: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment: Security DB authoritative for employment type, contractor with basic training, max is read.

So there's a conflict between HR (full_time) and Security (contractor). Security says their DB is authoritative for employment type.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic security training: max = read.
Requested admin > read, so grant read.

If full-time Engineer: max = write (admin only if role owns system; Engineer doesn't own Payroll). Requested admin > write, grant write.

So the decision hinges on employment type. Security agent says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. The Security note says contractor. So I should go with contractor, basic training -> max read. Grant read.

The final decision: read.

I'll submit read with reasoning.
